correctness.rationale: The 27 classical line classes give a uniform intersection table for all smooth cubic surfaces over the stated algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. I independently enumerated the sixers by recursively extending pairwise-skew sets. The six lines meeting five members of a given sixer are its unique partner, with one missing intersection in every row and column. Partnering is a fixed-point-free involution on 72 sixers and produces 36 distinct twelve-line supports. The graph has degrees 16 and 12; direct exact integer Smith and cofactor determinant computations with FLINT at a line sink and a double-six sink give 1^12,2^28,4^2,60,180^5,540^2,1080^6,4320^6 and determinant 2^96 * 3^53 * 5^20 at both sinks. This verifies connectedness, 432 edges, exponent 4320 and 50 minimum generators. The supplied exact local reduction is consistent: after splitting a unit pivot, dividing an all-divisible active block by p shifts every remaining valuation by one. No assertion about Picard torsion follows.
residual_risks: Uses the classical blow-up classification within the stated field regime; no arithmetic descent or positive-characteristic extension was tested.

value.rationale: The complete line–double-six flag graph is canonical, attaching all lines to a distinguished W(E6)-homogeneous family. Its integral degree-zero divisor quotient is a natural target for comparing chip-firing on different cubic-surface configurations. In particular the six order-4320 factors and the unusually large 2-primary generator rank are not recovered from the earlier order-four incidence obstruction or a tree count. The precise group can be used as reference data for integral or equivariant graph calculations, without claiming an equivariant decomposition here.
residual_risks: One fixed graph; no broader surface invariant or downstream theorem is established.
